title: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head M (Ministry of Finance)

sections.label: Revenue growth and NIRC
sections.summary: Revenue including NIRC grew about two times in 10 years, while operating revenue grew about one time without NIRC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On the other hand, our revenue, inclusive of Net Investment Return Contribution (NIRC), grew by about two times in the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If NIRC is excluded, our operating revenue would have only grown by about one time in the last one decade.

sections.label: NIRC share of total revenue
sections.summary: NIRC accounts for about one-fifth of total revenue, as the Minister for Finance said earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: NIRC now accounts for about one‐fifth of our total revenue, as the Minister for Finance has said earlier.

sections.label: Spending trajectory and fiscal sustainability
sections.summary: The question asks how MOF views the spending trajectory in the next five to 10 years and how fiscal sustainability is ensured.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Can the Minister shed some light as to how the Ministry of Finance (MOF) sees the spending trajectory in the next five to 10 years and how do we ensure fiscal sustainability?

sections.label: Spending exceeding revenue since 2015
sections.summary: Singapore has spent more than its revenue base since 2015, relying heavily on NIRC, which provided 21% of total expenditure in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, Singapore has been incurring more spending than its revenue base since 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have come to rely heavily on contributions from NIRC as the top contributor to spending needs, providing 21% of total expenditure in 2018.

sections.label: GIC 20-year annualised returns
sections.summary: GIC's 20-year annualised real return was 3.4% for the year ended 31 March 2018, after 3.7% and 4% in the prior two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the year ended 31 March 2018, GIC achieved the 20-year annualised rate of return of 3.4% above global inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The year before that, the rate of return was 3.7%, and for the year ended 31 March 2016, it was 4%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This constitutes three consecutive years of decline from the 4.7% at the end of 31 March 2015.

sections.label: Replacing CPF tax relief
sections.summary: Replacing CPF tax relief with a flat $250 top-up and 3% match could give the lowest-income deciles over $200 a month.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: Consider replacing CPF tax relief with a flat annual CPF top‐up of $250 and a 3% match on contributions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: In terms of retirement income, this could give the lowest-income deciles more than $200 a month, while cutting the benefit to the top decile from over $1,000 a month to about $500 a month.

sections.label: Private hire cars versus taxis
sections.summary: There are now two private hire cars to one taxi, compared with 28,500 taxis and no private hire cars five years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On the road today, there are now two private hire cars to one taxi, an alarming jump, considering that five years ago, we had 28,500 taxis and no private hire cars.

sections.label: Hired trips and vehicle growth
sections.summary: With 65,000 taxis and private hire cars, daily hired trips rose only from about one million to slightly over 1.2 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Those are about $20 more expensive than the diesel-driven taxis per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, with 65,000 taxis and private hire cars on the road, the size of the daily hired trips only increased marginally from about one million when we had 28,000 taxis, to slightly over 1.2 million currently, meaning that the number of commuting public that took either taxis or private hire cars, did not grow in tandem with the growth in total vehicles serving them.

sections.label: Procurement rules and innovation
sections.summary: Procurement rules need to evolve from prescriptive to more principles-based to better support innovation and enterprise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: Procurement rules need to be evolved from being prescriptive to being more principles‐based so as to better support innovation and enterprise.

sections.label: Lifecycle approach and Budget growth
sections.summary: The Budget increased from around $40 billion in 2007 to around $80 billion this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Could the Government adopt a lifecycle approach to evaluate more projects?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, our Budget has increased from around $40 billion in 2007 to around $80 billion this year.

sections.label: MOF on achieving balance
sections.summary: It asks whether MOF can share how the Government intends to achieve this balance moving forward.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can MOF share on how, moving forward, the Government intends to achieve this balance?

sections.label: Government expenditure share of GDP
sections.summary: Overall Government expenditure is around 19% of GDP, less than half of what many developed-country governments spend.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Our overall Government expenditure is around 19% of gross domestic product (GDP), less than half of what many governments of developed countries spend.

sections.label: Healthcare spending doubled over decade
sections.summary: Healthcare spending more than doubled over the last decade, reaching $10 billion in FY2018.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Already, our healthcare spending has more than doubled over the last decade to $10 billion in FY2018.

sections.label: NIRC and revenue sources
sections.summary: Without NIRC there would have been overall Budget deficits in each of the last 10 years; in FY2018 NIRC and corporate tax each contributed around 18% of total Government revenue.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: As both Members noted, we would have had overall Budget deficits in each of these last 10 years without the inclusion of NIRC.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In FY2018, NIRC and corporate tax contributed around 18% each to total Government revenue, followed closely by personal income tax and GST, each of which accounted for around 13% of total Government revenue.

sections.label: GIC five-year nominal return
sections.summary: Over a five-year timeframe, GIC's nominal return was 6.6% in US dollar nominal terms.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Over a five-year timeframe, GIC's nominal return was 6.6% in US dollar nominal terms.

sections.label: SRS tax savings contributions
sections.summary: In Singapore's context, for every $1 of tax savings enjoyed, $7 is contributed to SRS on average.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In the case of SRS, in Singapore's context, for every $1 of tax savings enjoyed, $7 is contributed to SRS on average.

sections.label: Relief cap and retirement support
sections.summary: These reliefs are subject to an overall personal income tax relief cap of $80,000, while the Government provides support such as Workfare, higher CPF interest and top-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, these reliefs are subject to an overall personal income tax relief cap of $80,000.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Government provides substantial support to help the lower- to middle-income achieve a more secure retirement.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These include Workfare which helps to build up CPF savings, higher CPF interest for the first $30,000 and $60,000 of CPF balances, and top-ups to CPF and MediSave accounts.

sections.label: Dependent parent tax reliefs
sections.summary: Tax reliefs of up to $9,000 per parent or $14,000 per handicapped parent are available for the support of dependent elderly parents.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Tax reliefs of up to $9,000 per parent or $14,000 per handicapped parent are available for the support of dependent elderly parents.

sections.label: Concessionary levy for FDW families
sections.summary: Families hiring FDWs for children, disabled or elderly members pay a $60 concessionary levy instead of the standard $265.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Families which hire FDWs to take care of children, household members with disabilities or elderly family members pay a concessionary levy of $60 instead of the standard $265.

sections.label: Deemed expense ratio for drivers
sections.summary: PHC and taxi drivers may claim tax deduction on a deemed expense ratio of 60% of gross driving income.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To further reduce record-keeping burden and administrative costs, we allow both PHC and taxi drivers to claim tax deduction on a deemed expense ratio at 60% of their gross driving income.

sections.label: Special Tax reduction for taxis
sections.summary: The Special Tax reduction for taxis is expected to permanently cover more than 75% of the cost impact to drivers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Special Tax reduction for taxis is expected to permanently cover more than 75% of the cost impact to drivers.

sections.label: Five-year development expenditure total
sections.summary: Over the past five years, total development expenditure amounted to $91 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, total development expenditure amounted to $91 billion.

sections.label: Savings from project reviews
sections.summary: Over five years, reviews led to design improvements and savings of about $3 billion, or 6% of initial estimated project value.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Over the past five years, these reviews have led to design improvements and generated savings of about $3 billion or 6% of the initial estimated value of the projects reviewed.

sections.label: ICT project review committee savings
sections.summary: A committee reviews project scope and system design for cost-effectiveness and integration, saving almost $800 million, over 5% of ICT spending, in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This committee reviews the project scope and system design to ensure that our ICT projects are cost-effective and well-integrated across the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This has helped us save almost $800 million, or over 5% of our ICT spending, over the past five years.

sections.label: Thomson-East Coast Line construction space
sections.summary: LTA officers worked with a condominium's management corporation to use space temporarily, reducing traffic diversions from 10 to three.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For instance, when constructing the Thomson-East Coast Line, LTA officers worked with the management corporation of a condominium to use some space within the condominium’s perimeter temporarily, so as to reduce the number of traffic diversions required from 10 to three.

sections.label: JTC security and GSR changes
sections.summary: JTC cut security manpower 25% and projected savings up to 40%; audited accounts requirement was removed for suppliers under $5 million turnover, and the quotation limit will rise to $90,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: As a result, JTC achieved better security coverage for the estate, alongside 25% security manpower reduction and projected cost savings of up to 40% over the contract period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Last year, we removed the requirement for companies with less than $5 million turnover to submit audited accounts when applying for Government Supplier Registration (GSR).

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: About 3,900 GSR-registered suppliers have benefited from this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This year, we will increase the upper limit for Quotations from $70,000 to $90,000.

sections.label: Virtual AGMs and Companies Act review
sections.summary: HP and PayPal adopted virtual AGMs citing reduced cost, and this year the Companies Act will be reviewed to provide for digital meetings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Fortune 500 companies like Hewlett-Packard (HP) Inc and PayPal have adopted virtual AGMs, citing reduced cost.

sentences.speaker: The Minister in the Prime Minister's Office, Second Minister for Education and Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This year, we will review the Companies Act to expressly provide for the use of digital means for companies to conduct meetings and interact with stakeholders.

sections.label: SRS tax cost and savings study
sections.summary: A Member asked whether the $1 tax cost to $7 retirement savings estimate accounts for diversion from taxable savings, and the Ministry will study this further.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Minister Lawrence Wong noted that $1 of tax cost in SRS leads to about $7 of retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: I want to ask if this estimate accounts for the diversion of retirement savings from taxable savings accounts to non-taxable.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
sentences.text: So, could the Ministry continue studying this with a view to understanding how the marginal new savings dollar is actually affected by the policy?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But I do not believe it has fully accounted for the effects that the Member has described.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We do need to do more detailed studies and we will engage in this.

sections.label: Utilisation rate projections and amendment withdrawal
sections.summary: The utilisation rate was in line with projections at the time of an earlier Parliamentary Question, monitoring will continue, and the amendment was withdrawn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, actually I believe we had answered a Parliamentary Question on this some time back.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I have not looked at the latest data, but at the time of that question, when we looked at the figures, the utilisation rate was, indeed, in line with projections as of that time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We make assumptions on these projections and so we will continue to monitor the utilisation, the assumptions that we have used and whether they are still relevant, and we will continue to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: As there are no other clarifications, Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: I believe we have a pretty good accumulated surplus for our COS time now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.
